# YourScreenHabits

> An educational digital wellbeing platform about healthy screen habits — what they are, how they affect sleep, eyes, focus, movement, mood and everyday routines, and how to build healthier ones. Created by students at Pak Turk Maarif Chak Shahzad Campus, Islamabad, Pakistan. Central belief: we don't ban the phone, we make the phone the scoreboard. The student campaign and British Council Your World 2026-27 competition are the origin and real-world application of the platform, not its whole identity. Free to read, no account needed, no competition, no award.

## Destinations

- [Home](https://yourscreenhabits.com/): what digital wellbeing means, why habits matter, the six health effects, featured guides, healthier habits, research, and the awareness initiative.
- [Understand Screen Habits](https://yourscreenhabits.com/#/understand): what screen habits are, purposes of use, active vs passive use, intentional vs automatic scrolling, why screen time alone does not tell the whole story, recognising unhealthy patterns.
- [Health & Effects](https://yourscreenhabits.com/#/health): sleep and night-time screen use, eyes and digital eye strain, focus and distractions, physical health and movement, mental wellbeing, everyday routines and dependency.
- [Healthy Habits](https://yourscreenhabits.com/#/habits): phone-free breaks, the 9pm screen cut-off, sleep and the last hour, reducing scrolling, managing notifications, eye breaks and posture, balancing screens with activity, offline time, intentional habits.
- [Guides & Resources](https://yourscreenhabits.com/#/guides): thirteen articles and topics — seven guides and six health topics — each ending with one habit to try for seven days.
- [Research & Expert Insights](https://yourscreenhabits.com/#/research): WHO guidance, American Academy of Pediatrics guidance, research on sleep, eye strain and physical activity, and references. No interviews have been conducted yet.
- [About Us](https://yourscreenhabits.com/#/about): the story, mission, team, school, awareness activities, British Council Your World 2026-27, and how impact is measured.
- [Newsletter](https://yourscreenhabits.com/#/newsletter): digital wellbeing updates, new guides, campaign updates. Issue 1 lands 1 December 2026.
